key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves an aluminium MACE potential’s defect predictions while preserving its tested near-equilibrium mechanical and vibrational response.
engineering_relevance: The protocol supports more reliable atomistic simulations of aluminium defect dynamics and plasticity without sacrificing validated bulk behavior.
method: Select configurations using conditional readout uncertainty with within-batch covariance updates.
Iteratively update all model parameters while anchoring historical relative energies.
Gate model acceptance using historical elastic-group energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: Four active-learning rounds acquired 32 configurations over 400 gradient updates, reducing mean development force error from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å; all three force-uncertainty runs met bulk-retention criteria, with phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested aluminium responses; broader deployment requires additional validation, and the closed-loop MD–DFT result remains a pilot.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
